observed_source_claims: AgentCgroup studies OS-level resource behavior across 144 SWE-rebench software-engineering tasks and two LLM models.

The paper reports OS-level execution as 56-74 percent of end-to-end task latency, memory as the principal concurrency bottleneck in the studied setting, and tool-call-driven memory spikes up to 15.4x peak-to-average.
The implementation aligns ephemeral child cgroups with tool-call boundaries and combines cgroup-v2 hierarchy with sched_ext CPU control and memcg_bpf_ops memory control.

The bash wrapper can associate each command with a tool-call resource domain, record duration/peak memory/exit/hint fields, clean up the child cgroup, and expose an OOM/resource-pressure signal back to the agent.

Real control experiments require Linux/cgroup/eBPF capabilities including root access; the source documents Linux 6.12+ sched_ext and cgroup v2, while some memory-control mechanisms have stronger kernel coupling than ordinary portable user-space telemetry.
The repository also contains trace replay and analysis paths, so characterization can be separated from live enforcement.

f2_architecture_implications.hypothesis: F2 should measure resource use at exact tool-call/effect-attempt identity rather than relying only on aggregate session averages.
f2_architecture_implications.candidate_native_distillation: A typed ToolResourceReceipt bound to run/session/tool_call/generation/provenance with start/end time, exit class, peak/current memory, CPU time where available, I/O/network counters where available, declared resource request, admitted budget decision, and OOM/kill/throttle observations.
f2_architecture_implications.reason: The external evidence indicates highly bursty per-tool-call resource behavior; a typed receipt can preserve the useful granularity without importing AgentCgroup as a second control authority.

f2_architecture_implications.hypothesis: Agent-declared resource hints may be useful predictions but must never self-grant resources or canonical capability.
f2_architecture_implications.candidate_native_distillation: Treat a resource hint as untrusted candidate input; deterministic F2 budget/capability authority validates, narrows or rejects it and records the decision separately from the hint.

f2_architecture_implications.hypothesis: Resource pressure should re-enter cognition as typed observed evidence, not as free-form textual authority.
f2_architecture_implications.candidate_native_distillation: Canonical receipt records observed OOM/kill/throttle/limit event; any natural-language recovery suggestion is a projection/candidate strategy only.

f2_architecture_implications.hypothesis: A measurement-only phase has higher portability and lower architecture risk than immediately adopting an eBPF resource scheduler/controller.
f2_architecture_implications.candidate_native_distillation: First bind tool-call resource telemetry and replayable receipts to existing F2 effect/tool identities; only consider active resource enforcement after native traces show a material bottleneck that simpler cgroup/user-space controls cannot handle.

negative_adoption_decisions: Do not import AgentCgroup, sched_ext policy, memcg_bpf_ops controller, daemon, or bash replacement as F2 canonical resource authority from E1 evidence.
Do not grant F2 performance, portability, isolation or overhead credit from AgentCgroup's upstream measurements.
Do not treat agent-generated AGENT_RESOURCE_HINT values as authoritative budgets or capabilities.
Do not treat upstream README experiment counts or preliminary paper evaluation as independent F2 reproduction.
Do not execute privileged eBPF/cgroup experiments under the current Clay FREE_ONLY execution boundary.
counterhypotheses: F2 may not need tool-call-level resource enforcement at its target deployment; ordinary process/container telemetry may already be sufficient for diagnosis and capacity planning.
The bookkeeping cost of a rich ToolResourceReceipt may outweigh value for very short tool calls unless sampling and field requirements are bounded.
Memory burstiness measured on SWE-rebench coding agents may not transfer to F2 workloads, so F2 must measure its own distributions before changing scheduling architecture.
A standard cgroup-v2 or process-level observer may reproduce most useful measurement value without eBPF or custom-kernel coupling.

e2_discriminator.question: Can existing F2 telemetry/effect identities support a minimal tool-call resource receipt without a new authority or privileged controller?
e2_discriminator.method: Static architecture map current F2 telemetry/effect/resource paths against the minimal ToolResourceReceipt fields; identify reusable identities and missing fields. No runtime/eBPF execution.
e2_discriminator.pass_for_build_candidate: A thin derived/native receipt can bind exact tool/effect attempt identity, generation/provenance and observed resource outcomes while preserving existing deterministic authority boundaries.
e2_discriminator.reject_or_defer: If existing telemetry already provides equivalent exact fields, record redundancy; if resource identity cannot bind cleanly without a second authority, defer and repair identity first.

efficiency_note: The strongest transferable idea is granularity and evidence binding, not the full controller. Prefer a small F2-native receipt/observer over a privileged daemon plus scheduler unless later F2 measurements falsify that simpler design.
next_exact_action: Acquire a create-only R6-SEED-006/E2_ARCHITECTURE_MAPPED claim if absent, then statically map the minimal ToolResourceReceipt onto current F2 tool/effect/telemetry/resource identities and emit either a thin build candidate or an explicit redundancy/defer result.
